The Guardian (Jessica Elgot, Deputy political editor) — published Sat 26 Sep 2026, 06:00 BST (Sat 26 Sep 2026 01.00 EDT)

HEADLINE: Labour must reunite progressive voters to win the next election, says Lucy Powell
Standfirst: The deputy leader wants the party to take advantage of a split on the right and not be embarrassed to show its values

Labour must "reunite the progressive voter coalition" if it is to take advantage of a split on the right and win the next election, the party's deputy leader Lucy Powell has said. Powell won the race to be deputy leader 12 months ago with a warning that Labour was losing the fight to be heard.

NOTE: article body retrieved only partially (fetch truncated after the opening paragraphs). The verified verbatim phrase is "reunite the progressive voter coalition". The Guardian describes Powell as "the party's deputy leader"; The Independent's PA copy the same day describes her as "Education Secretary Lucy Powell" — both titles appear in approved-source copy today.
